original_question: For every k >= 1 and every n >= 3, does there exist a k-orbit n-polytope with no rank-2 section that is a digon?
target_in_paper: The closest paper-faithful target is the open existence problem asking whether every pair (k,n) with k >= 1 and n >= 3 can be realized by a non-degenerate k-orbit abstract n-polytope.
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the main quantifiers right ('for every k >= 1' and 'every n >= 3'), it is clearly about k-orbit n-polytopes, and it correctly encodes the intended non-degeneracy condition by excluding rank-2 sections that are digons.
missing_details: The paper’s setting is abstract polytopes, so the question should explicitly say 'abstract n-polytope.'
The term 'k-orbit' should be made stand-alone: it means that the automorphism group has exactly k orbits on flags.
The condition 'no rank-2 section that is a digon' is best identified with the standard shorthand 'non-degenerate,' if that terminology is introduced nearby.
The draft does not say whether finiteness is intended; in the paper’s general abstract-polytope setting, that should not be added unless the local context explicitly imposes it.
The question should make clear that this is a purely combinatorial existence problem, not a convex or geometric realization problem.
Ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, and nilpotency conditions are not applicable here, because the problem is not algebraic.
refined_question: For every integers k >= 1 and n >= 3, does there exist a non-degenerate abstract n-polytope P whose automorphism group has exactly k orbits on the flags of P?
equivalent_formulation: For every integers k >= 1 and n >= 3, does there exist a k-orbit abstract n-polytope with no rank-2 section isomorphic to a digon?
justification: This paper is an open-problems survey on k-orbit abstract polytopes, and the accessible author materials tied to it fix the relevant language: abstract n-polytopes are the ambient objects, and a k-orbit polytope is one with k flag-orbits under its automorphism group. Your draft is already very close to the intended problem; the main sharpening is to make 'abstract' and 'flag-orbits' explicit and to compress the digon-exclusion hypothesis into the standard term 'non-degenerate' when presenting the final stand-alone question. I did not broaden the question to geometric, convex, or skeletal realizations, since the draft is plainly about the abstract-combinatorial existence problem.
